newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- easing while Fed-waiting.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- easing while Fed-waiting.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were easier at the short-end and narrowly mixed at the long end in early afternoon trade, as the market waited to see if the Federal Reserve would elect to raise interest rates.

"I think the short-end is off an 0.05, the long end is off an 0.01, and we're probably unchanged," said an intermediate trader. He noted that long-end traders said some bonds in this sector gained slightly.

The recent flattening in the yield curve suggested that the market does not see runaway inflation, but traders remained edgy that the central bank still might see enough of a threat to act aggressively.
Activity largely dried up as Federal policy-makers met. The central bank was expected to make its announcment at approximately 1415 EDT.

Traders said that even though municipal bonds recently have outperformed Treasuries, small retail accounts were noticeable by their absence. But traders were not ready to say municipals were due for a near-term correction.
"I think it's insane," a trader said, adding municipals did not seem to be fairly valued even though dwindling supplies have helped propel their prices higher.
He calculated that municipal bonds represent 79.5 percent of Treasuries, well below the more typical 82 to 83 percent level. "Relative value is not that good, you're not building in any protection."
Later, he added: "You tend to see some relationship between how wide the spread gets and how much business you do," as activity picks up when the spread is narrower.
But the trader noted that municipals have been known to linger at levels that can seem overbought.
Much of the market's attention was focused on Nevada's sale of $285 million of general obligation bonds, which were won by Smith Barney with a true interest cost of 5.53 percent.
And traders also were waiting to see how many New York City bonds were sold to individual investors during the presale period that ended at 1300 EDT.

In the first two days of the presale period, the city appeared to be falling short of a previous mark, as it had only sold about $133 million by late Monday. New York City sells about $750 million of bonds on Wednesday.
June U.S. Treasury futures fell eight ticks to 109-21/32, while June municipal futures eased three ticks to 116-14/32. This left the MOB spread at a rich plus 218 ticks.
In the secondary market, Lorain County, Ohio, Hospital Revenues of 2027, which pay a 5-1/2 percent coupon, were bid at 5.78 percent, NET, up two basis points.
And Massachusetts State Port Authority Revenues of 2027, which have a 5-5/8 percent coupon, were offered at 5.85 percent, NET, unchanged.
